title: Geometric fibre dimension bounds for algebraic spaces under base change
statement: Algebraic spaces and their morphisms are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], over schemes [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $f:X\to T$ be a morphism from an algebraic space to a scheme, locally of finite type on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and quasi-separated (its diagonal $X\to X\times_TX$ is quasi-compact), and let $d\geq0$ be an integer. Write $P_d(f)$ for the condition that every geometric fibre has topological Krull dimension at most $d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. A geometric fibre here is the algebraic-space fibre product $X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ for a map from the spectrum of an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-weil-affine-spectrum, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; the dimension is that of its underlying topological space. Quasi-separatedness makes every geometric fibre a quasi-separated, hence decent, algebraic space, so this topological dimension is the dimension computed on etale charts. If $P_d(f)$ holds, then $P_d(X\times_TT'\to T')$ holds for every scheme map $T'\to T$. Conversely, for any jointly surjective family of scheme maps $\{T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$, if $P_d(X\times_TT_i\to T_i)$ holds for every $i$, then $P_d(f)$ holds. Joint surjectivity means every point of $T$ is in the image of some $T_i$.

proof.text: First note that the geometric fibres used below remain quasi-separated and locally of finite type over their fields. Indeed the diagonal of $X\times_TZ\to Z$ is the pullback of $\Delta_{X/T}$ along $(X\times_TZ)\times_Z(X\times_TZ)\to X\times_TX$. After any scheme test this is a base change of a quasi-compact scheme morphism, hence is quasi-compact by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change]. Pulling back an etale atlas gives an etale atlas by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The chart morphisms to $Z$ are base changes of the original locally finite type chart morphisms, and remain locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change]. This works for every scheme $Z\to T$, including field spectra; no condition on $Z\to T$ is used.

proof.text: Let $T'\to T$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T'$ be arbitrary, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. The universal property of the sheaf fibre products gives $(X\times_TT')\times_{T'}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\cong X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$: on every test scheme both sides are pairs of compatible maps to $X$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. The right hand side is one of the geometric fibres quantified over in $P_d(f)$, so has dimension at most $d$. The isomorphism identifies the atlas topologies and hence their chains of irreducible closed subsets. This proves the base-change implication.

We need a field-extension comparison for the converse. Let $Y$ be a quasi-separated algebraic space locally of finite type over a field $k$, and $L/k$ any extension. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to Y$. Its pullback $U_L\to Y_L$ is again such an atlas, and $Y_L$ is quasi-separated by Step 1. By [lem-sfb-quasiseparated-space-atlas-dimension], $\dim|Y|=\dim U$ and $\dim|Y_L|=\dim U_L$. The chart $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type. Apply [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] to $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Both bases have one point with residue fields $k$ and $L$, so its two scheme fibres are exactly $U$ and $U_L$. It gives $\dim_{u'}U_L=\dim_uU$ for every $u'\mapsto u$. These are the local topological dimensions used in the supremum formula: both [def-kun-dimension] and [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] define them as the minimum dimensions of open neighbourhoods, not dimensions of local rings. The projection $U_L\to U$ is surjective by [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Thus the two sets of attained local dimensions coincide. Taking their suprema by [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] gives $\dim U_L=\dim U$, hence $\dim|Y_L|=\dim|Y|$. For empty atlases both suprema are $-\infty$.

proof.text: Assume all the $P_d(f_i)$ and fix $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed and image $t$. Joint surjectivity gives $i$ and $t_i\in T_i$ over $t$. The residue-field maps make both $\Omega$ and $\kappa(t_i)$ extensions of $\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. By [lem-weil-common-extension-fields] embed them over $\kappa(t)$ in a common field $M$; by [def-weil-algebraic-closure] enlarge $M$ to an algebraically closed field $L$. The induced $\operatorname{Spec}L\to T_i$ and $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ have equal composites to $T$, since both factor through $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ with the same field map. Fibre-product associativity therefore identifies $X_{\bar t}\times_\Omega L$ with the geometric fibre $(X\times_TT_i)\times_{T_i}\operatorname{Spec}L$. Its dimension is at most $d$ by $P_d(f_i)$. Apply Step 3 to the quasi-separated locally finite type $\Omega$-space $X_{\bar t}$ to conclude $\dim|X_{\bar t}|\leq d$. Since $\bar t$ was arbitrary, $P_d(f)$ follows. If the covering family is empty, joint surjectivity forces $T$ empty and there are no geometric points to check.

lean.statement: theorem geometricFibreDimensionLE_baseChange_and_descent {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (T : Over S) (f : X.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T) (hft : MapToSchemeIsLocally (@LocallyOfFiniteType) X T f) (hqs : MapIsQuasiCompact (Limits.pullback.diagonal f)) (d : ℕ) : (GeometricFibreDimensionLE T f d → ∀ (T' : Over S) (g : T' ⟶ T), GeometricFibreDimensionLE T' (Limits.pullback.snd f (yoneda.map g)) d) ∧ (∀ (I : Type w) (Tᵢ : I → Over S) (g : ∀ i : I, Tᵢ i ⟶ T), (∀ t : T.left, ∃ (i : I) (tᵢ : (Tᵢ i).left), (g i).left tᵢ = t) → (∀ i : I, GeometricFibreDimensionLE (Tᵢ i) (Limits.pullback.snd f (yoneda.map (g i))) d) → GeometricFibreDimensionLE T f d)
